children: The field-weighted relevance function the Indx Engine ranks with — title outranks body, computed natively rather than borrowed from Postgres.

BM25F is the field-aware variant of BM25. Where plain BM25 scores a document as one bag of words, BM25F splits it into fields and weights each one before combining — in Barkpark that means a title match counts for more than a body match. The Indx Engine uses BM25F as its core ranking signal across the Document corpus.

Postgres Search reaches a similar "title beats body" outcome by a different mechanism: it runs ts_rank over the Search Vector, whose weight classes (A for title down to D for body) are baked in at index time via setweight. BM25F applies its field weights at query time, so they can be tuned without rebuilding an index — Postgres bakes them into a generated column that only a Migration can recompute.

| Aspect | BM25F (Indx Engine) | ts_rank (Postgres Search) | |---|---|---| | Field weights | query-time, tunable | index-time via setweight | | Fuzziness | native | pg_trgm widen | | Facets | native | GROUP BY |

Both engines sit behind the one Search contract and return identical Search Facets. They also share the upstream Auto Correction Loop and Synonyms expansion, so a learned correction reaches BM25F and ts_rank alike. Which engine wins on a given query mix is settled empirically by the Golden Eval harness — and the clickstream in Search Intelligence is where a future re-rank of these field weights would draw its training signal.
